analystSummary.en: Proposition 3 makes the higher income tax rates established by Proposition 30 permanent instead of letting them expire in 2031. Figure 1 shows what income tax rates would be if this measure passes and what they would be if it is rejected.

fiscalEffect.en: Maintains $5 billion to $15 billion of annual state income tax revenue by making a temporary tax increase on high-income earners permanent instead of letting it expire in 2031.

funders.name: PACE of California School Employees Association-Issues

reason.en: The official summary says Proposition 3 "Makes permanent existing voter-approved tax rates for individuals earning over $371,000 (adjusted annually for inflation)." A YES vote keeps a rate already in place rather than adding a new tax, so this link shows no direction.

noMeans.en: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would expire in 2031.

officialTitle.en: Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.

sourceTitle.en: Official Voter Information Guide, November 3, 2026 General Election: Proposition 3, certified August 10, 2026

yesMeans.en: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would become permanent instead of expiring in 2031.
